name: Mycoplasma encephalitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed criteria for Mycoplasma encephalitis diagnosis

criteria.description: Acute onset of neurological symptoms including altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurological deficits
Laboratory evidence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection (serology or PCR positive)
CSF pleocytosis or elevated protein consistent with encephalitis
MRI findings suggestive of encephalitis such as T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in cerebral white matter or basal ganglia
Exclusion of other infectious or autoimmune causes of encephalitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of acute neurological symptoms plus laboratory evidence of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection and CSF abnormalities consistent with encephalitis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by laboratory and imaging findings; exclusion of other causes is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Altered mental status with confusion or decreased consciousness
Seizures including focal or generalized convulsions
Focal neurological deficits such as hemiparesis or cranial nerve palsies

common.symptomName: Headache of moderate to severe intensity

occasional.symptomName: Behavioral changes including irritability or agitation
Limb weakness without clear focal deficit
searchTerms: weak arms or legs without specific nerve loss

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms such as cough or mild dyspnea preceding neurological signs
searchTerms: cough or mild breathing trouble before neurological symptoms

rare.symptomName: Optic neuritis leading to visual impairment
searchTerms: blurred or lost vision from nerve inflammation

rare.symptomName: Autonomic dysfunction including blood pressure instability

laboratory: Positive Mycoplasma pneumoniae serology (IgM and/or IgG)
PCR detection of Mycoplasma pneumoniae DNA in respiratory or CSF samples
imaging: MRI brain showing T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, or brainstem
Possible meningeal enhancement on contrast MRI
other: Electroencephalogram (EEG) may show diffuse slowing or epileptiform discharges
Exclusion of other infectious agents by CSF PCR panels

distinguishingFeatures: Rapid progression with temporal lobe involvement on MRI
More common in adults and elderly
Often subacute onset with prominent psychiatric symptoms
Identification of other viral pathogens (e.g., enterovirus, arboviruses)

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema or severe headache
references: Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases, 9th Edition, Mycoplasma pneumoniae infections
Mycoplasma pneumoniae-associated encephalitis: clinical features and outcomes, Journal of Neurology, 2020
Encephalitis: Clinical features and diagnosis, UpToDate, 2024
